request_context: A request to find the security threats in a described system design and map controls to them, as a threat model a security reviewer can check.

rules.source_quote: Use consistent threat numbering (T-001, T-002, etc.)
rules.outcome: Numbers threats T-001 onward and mitigations M-001 onward.

rules.source_quote: Never assume or infer the existence of security controls, services, or architecture components not clearly specified
rules.outcome: Does not add components or controls the design does not state (a WAF, a VPC, encryption) and does not credit them.
rules.scenario_hint: A design that lists few controls.

rules.source_quote: Leaks usually happen in URLs, headers, logs, and emails, not in the primary store
rules.outcome: Traces each token, secret and credential through the flow and flags where it leaks: in URLs, headers, logs or emails.
rules.why: Most leaks are in transit paths, not the database.
rules.scenario_hint: A flow with presigned links, tokens or API keys.

rules.source_quote: rating each threat's likelihood and impact and deriving its priority from both
rules.outcome: Gives each threat a likelihood and an impact rating, and a priority that follows from both.
rules.why: Priority without both ratings is a guess.

rules.source_quote: Do not mark something Implemented because it is a common default
rules.outcome: Marks each mitigation Implemented only when the design documents it, and Not implemented or Unknown otherwise.
rules.why: Assumed defaults are a common gap.
rules.scenario_hint: A design silent on a usual default such as encryption.

rules.source_quote: State each mitigation as a concrete change to this design
rules.outcome: Writes each mitigation as a concrete change to a named component or setting, not consider X.
rules.why: Vague mitigations do not get built.

rules.source_quote: Security testing strategy as a table: test ID, type, the concrete input or action, expected result, and the threat IDs it covers
rules.outcome: Gives a test table with test id, type, concrete input, expected result and the threat ids covered.
rules.why: Tests tied to threats prove mitigations work.
rules.scenario_hint: A request that asks how to test.

rules.source_quote: Ensure each threat has at least one mitigation
rules.outcome: Maps every threat to at least one mitigation.
rules.why: An unmitigated threat is an open risk.

rules.source_quote: each in-scope component against the six categories
rules.outcome: Gives a coverage matrix of each in-scope component against the six STRIDE categories, with threat ids or none found in each cell.

rules.source_quote: record each one in the document's assumptions table with what changes if it is wrong
rules.outcome: When asked not to ask questions, makes small assumptions and lists each in an assumptions table with what changes if it is wrong.
rules.why: Reviewers check assumptions in one place.
rules.scenario_hint: A request saying do not ask me questions.

rules.source_quote: model only what the change adds or alters
rules.outcome: For a change to an existing design, models only the new or changed parts and trust boundaries.
rules.why: Re-modelling the whole system buries the change.
rules.scenario_hint: A new endpoint added to an existing design.

rules.source_quote: Continue the threat and mitigation numbering from where the user says to start.
rules.outcome: Starts threat and mitigation numbers where the user says.
rules.why: Keeps ids unique across the document.
rules.scenario_hint: A change model told to start at T-021.

rules.outcome: Names the external trust boundaries (internet to API, third party callbacks) and analyses authentication and authorization threats at them.
rules.why: Missing boundaries is a must-fix gap.
rules.scenario_hint: A design with an internet-facing entry.

rules.source_quote: A launch recommendation: which mitigations must ship first
rules.outcome: Ends with residual risks and which mitigations must ship before launch.

rules.source_quote: Limit threat analysis to documented architecture within the defined scope boundaries
rules.outcome: Keeps the analysis to the stated scope.
rules.why: Any good analysis keeps to scope.

rules.source_quote: Data in transit and at rest encryption not addressed
rules.outcome: Addresses encryption in transit and at rest for each data store and link, flagging where the design is silent.
rules.why: Missing encryption analysis is a must-fix gap.
rules.scenario_hint: A design with stores and network links.
